strings.name: Mo Farah
strings.summary: Farah combined tactical patience with a fast finish to win both the 5,000 m and 10,000 m at London 2012 and Rio 2016, alongside six world titles. He later moved toward road racing and won the Chicago Marathon. In 2022 he disclosed being trafficked to Britain as a child under another person's name. After retiring in 2023, he continued advocating children's participation in sport.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through November 16, 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Multiple Olympic distance titles gave him a prominent influence in world athletics and British public sporting culture.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f1.value: Born in present-day Somaliland and trafficked to Britain as a child; his birth name was Hussein Abdi Kahin.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Two Olympic doubles
strings.highlights.h1.text: Won both 5,000 m and 10,000 m gold in 2012 and 2016.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education and early training
strings.facts.f2.value: Encouraged at school in London by PE teacher Alan Watkinson and trained with a running club.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Six world titles
strings.highlights.h2.text: Won six world championship gold medals across the two distances from 2011 to 2017.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Promotes children's sport
strings.timeline.t1.text: As a school sport advocate, encouraged children to be active daily.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Final professional race
strings.timeline.t2.text: Completed the Great North Run, ending his elite distance-running career.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Discloses childhood trafficking
strings.timeline.t3.text: A documentary recounted being trafficked to Britain and required to use another child's name.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Chicago Marathon victory
strings.timeline.t4.text: Won a World Marathon Majors race after moving toward road running.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Rio distance double
strings.timeline.t5.text: Repeated his London achievement by winning both distance titles.
strings.timeline.t6.title: World championship double
strings.timeline.t6.text: Won both the 5,000 m and 10,000 m world titles for the first time in Moscow.
strings.timeline.t7.title: London Olympic double
strings.timeline.t7.text: Won both distance titles at his home Olympics.
strings.timeline.t8.title: First world title
strings.timeline.t8.text: Won the 5,000 m and took 10,000 m silver in Daegu.
strings.timeline.t9.title: Begins club training
strings.timeline.t9.text: Joined Newham and Essex Beagles and progressed toward competitive distance running.
